### SRC-001 — Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (statute)

- Issuing body: United States Congress
- Authority type: statute
- Citation: 20 U.S.C. 1232g
- Locator: https://studentprivacy.ed.gov/ferpa
- Version: As codified, U.S. Code current edition; effective 1974-08-21
- Verified: 2026-08-19 by Primary-source retrieval (studentprivacy.ed.gov, govinfo CFR annual edition cross-check)
- Status: VERIFIED-CURRENT; lifecycle EFFECTIVE
- Locators used: 20 U.S.C. 1232g(a); 20 U.S.C. 1232g(b)

**What the source states.** Conditions federal funding on educational agencies and institutions granting parents and eligible students access to education records and restricting disclosure of personally identifiable information without written consent.

**Reproduction boundary.** Summarised. No statutory text is reproduced in SSLS artifacts; consult the cited source for operative language.

**Note.** Binds educational agencies and institutions, not technology vendors, unless the vendor acts for the institution.

### SRC-002 — Family Educational Rights and Privacy (regulation)

- Issuing body: U.S. Department of Education
- Authority type: regulation
- Citation: 34 CFR Part 99
- Locator: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title34-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title34-vol1-part99.pdf

### SRC-007 — 603 CMR 23.00: Student Records

- Issuing body: Massachusetts Board of Elementary and Secondary Education
- Authority type: regulation
- Citation: 603 CMR 23.00
- Locator: https://www.doe.mass.edu/lawsregs/603cmr23.html
- Version: Most recently amended by the Board 2026-01-27; effective 2026-01-27
- Verified: 2026-08-19 by Direct retrieval from doe.mass.edu
- Status: VERIFIED-CURRENT; lifecycle EFFECTIVE
- Locators used: 603 CMR 23.01; 603 CMR 23.02; 603 CMR 23.03; 603 CMR 23.05; 603 CMR 23.06

**What the source states.** Governs Massachusetts student records: assigns rights by student age, defines authorized school personnel to include service-contract personnel with duty-limited access, requires the principal and superintendent to secure records including electronic systems, and sets destruction timelines of sixty years for the transcript and no later than seven years for the temporary record.

**Reproduction boundary.** Summarised only.

**Note.** Obligations are placed on the district. Vendor reach is contractual, not direct regulatory force.

### SRC-011 — 201 CMR 17.00: Standards for the Protection of Personal Information

- Issuing body: Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation
- Authority type: regulation
- Citation: 201 CMR 17.00
- Locator: https://www.mass.gov/doc/201-cmr-17-standards-for-the-protection-of-personal-information-of-residents-of-the-commonwealth/download
- Version: Current published edition; effective 2010-03-01
- Verified: 2026-08-19 by Direct retrieval and text extraction of the official mass.gov PDF
- Status: VERIFIED-CURRENT; lifecycle EFFECTIVE
- Locators used: 201 CMR 17.01; 201 CMR 17.02; 201 CMR 17.03(2)(f); 201 CMR 17.04

**What the source states.** Applies to all persons that own or license personal information about a Massachusetts resident, requires a written comprehensive information security program with enumerated administrative, technical and physical safeguards, requires oversight of third-party service providers by contract, and sets computer system security requirements including authentication, access control and encryption in transit and on portable devices.

**Reproduction boundary.** Summarised only. Clause-level detail of 17.04 subsections beyond (1)-(3) was not fully enumerated in the WP-038 pass.

**Note.** Personal information here means a name combined with SSN, driver's licence or state ID, or financial account number. This is narrower than FERPA education-record data.

### SRC-017 — ADA Title II web and mobile accessibility rule

- Issuing body: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
- Authority type: regulation
- Citation: 28 CFR Part 35 Subpart H; 89 FR 31320; 91 FR 20902
- Locator: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/04/24/2024-07758

**What the source states.** Requires public entities to make web content and mobile applications readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities, conforming to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to listed exceptions and limited defences.
